name: A Fun Guide to Food Spoilage!

pages.title: Your Steak is a Brick
pages.text: $(bold)Good news:$() You have food!$(br)$(bold)Bad news:$() It's frozen solid.$(br2)Starting in $(bold)Phase 4$(), food in your inventory accumulates $(italic)frost ticks$() when temperature drops below $(bold)-30°C$(). The colder it gets, the faster your food deteriorates.$(br2)$(italic)ORSA Nutritional Advisory: "Food is only food if you can chew it."$()

pages.title: Stage 1: "Chilled"
pages.text: At $(bold)600 frost ticks$() below -30°C (about 12 seconds at -90°C), your food becomes Chilled.$(br2)$(li)Tooltip shows frost status$(li)Still perfectly edible$(li)You're in denial. It's fine.$(br2)This is nature's way of telling you to eat now. You will not listen.$(br2)$(italic)ORSA Tip: If you're saving that steak "for later," later is going to be very disappointing.$()

pages.title: Stage 2: "Frozen"
pages.text: At $(bold)2,400 frost ticks$() (about 48 seconds at -90°C), your food hits Frozen.$(br2)$(li)$(bold)Eating takes 2x longer$(li)$(bold)Restores half hunger$() — ice crystals are not nutrition$(br2)You can still eat it. You'll just hate every second. Like reheated pizza, except it's -60°C and you're crying.$(br2)$(italic)Fun fact: At this temperature, bread has the structural integrity of concrete.$()

pages.title: Stage 3: "Frost-Ruined"
pages.text: At $(bold)6,000 frost ticks$() (about 2 minutes at -90°C), your food is Frost-Ruined.$(br2)$(li)$(bold)Completely inedible$(li)$(bold)Permanently damaged$() — thawing only recovers to Frozen$(br2)This isn't food anymore. It's a cold, crystallized monument to your failure to plan ahead.$(br2)$(italic)Staring at frost-ruined steak for more than 10 seconds may cause existential dread. This is normal.$()

pages.title: Thawing & Recovery
pages.text: Near heat sources (above $(bold)10°C$()), food gradually thaws:$(br2)$(li)$(bold)Mild heat$() (10-30°C): Slow recovery$(li)$(bold)Strong heat$() (30°C+): Fast recovery$(br2)Chilled and Frozen food can fully recover if thawed before Frost-Ruined. $(bold)Once Frost-Ruined, it only ever thaws back to Frozen.$(br2)$(italic)Science! It's like frostbite, but for steak.$()$(br2)Traveling? Use the $(l:getting_started/ration_warmer)ORSA Ration Warmer$(/l) for a ten-second whole-stack thaw and a thirty-second warm window.

pages.title: ORSA Ration Warmer
pages.text: Food in your $(bold)offhand.$() Warmer in your $(bold)main hand.$() Right-click once and wait.$(br2)One charge thaws the $(bold)entire stack in 10 seconds$(), regardless of ambient temperature. You can keep moving and put the warmer away. Keep the original food stack in your offhand. Progress appears above the hotbar.$(br2)ORSA advises against using the device as a pillow.
Four iron corners, four copper edges and redstone in the center. One reusable warmer, crafted $(bold)empty.$() No Nether ingredients required.

Craft the existing warmer with $(bold)1–4 redstone dust$() to add up to four charges. Dust can be stacked in one slot or spread across slots. One dust per charge, maximum $(bold)four.$() Only the missing charges are filled; excess dust stays in the grid. Device data is preserved.

pages.title: Field Service Limits
pages.text: Chilled and Frozen food returns to fresh. Frost-Ruined food only recovers to damaged Frozen; permanent damage remains.$(br2)Fresh and frost-resistant food cost no charge. Completed food gets $(bold)30 seconds$() before frost resumes. This device heats food only.$(br2)You can put the warmer away or switch hotbar slots. Keep the original full food stack in your offhand. Removing, replacing or splitting the food, dying, changing dimension or leaving cancels with $(bold)no refund.$()

pages.title: The Thermal Container
pages.text: The $(bold)Thermal Container$() — ORSA's patented food preservation unit!$(br2)$(li)Holds $(bold)8 food items$(li)$(bold)Fully insulates$() from frost ticks$(li)Doesn't stack (it's a lunchbox, not a pocket dimension)$(br2)$(italic)Kevin once tried to fit 9 steaks in one. The lid exploded. He still has the scar.$()
Iron for structure, leather for insulation, glass bottle for... science? Look, it works.

pages.title: Frost-Resistant Foods
pages.text: Some foods are naturally immune to frost:$(br2)$(li)$(bold)Golden Apples$() — gold doesn't freeze (it does, but these are magical)$(li)$(bold)Enchanted Golden Apples$() — literally glowing$(li)$(bold)Dried Kelp$() — already desiccated, nothing left to ruin$(li)$(bold)Hot Wings$() — blaze powder is apparently a valid preservation method$(br2)Everything else? $(italic)Fair game.$(br2)$(bold)Reminder:$() The thermal container exists. Use it.
